data.hypothesis: Packing each B reduction-by-column panel into compact scratch may improve panel locality while it is reused across the 32x64 output tile, enough to offset the packing and allocation cost. Keeping the parent’s tile sizes, loop order, serial execution, first-reduction overwrite, and scalar 4x4 microkernel otherwise unchanged makes this a packing-focused comparison; the result remains unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these as comparison points for the packing-only candidate; they do not establish the effect of packing.
memory_lessons.claim: The serial blocked 4x4 candidate was correct and measured 0.283056 s mean; the valid parallel-tile candidate measured 0.033899 s mean, and the baseline measured 6.405855 s mean. These are measured outcomes, not guarantees for this candidate.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare packing against the serial blocked parent on all official cases and repeated native n=1024 timings, including scratch allocation and copying in the timed call.

data.notes: The catalog contains two distinct valid programs: simple serial blocking at 0.283056 s mean and the parallel-tile variant at 0.033899 s mean; the baseline mean was 6.405855 s. This candidate adds compact B-panel packing to the selected serial parent without adding parallelism or explicit SIMD. It is unmeasured here; controller correctness checks and repeated native n=1024 timings are needed before drawing conclusions.
transformations: Retain the selected parent’s 32x64 output tiles, 64-element reduction blocks, scalar register-oriented 4x4 microkernel, and serial tile traversal.
Allocate a 64x64 B-panel scratch buffer inside run and pack each current B panel before computing its corresponding output tile, so allocation and copying remain in timed cost.
Read packed B values in both the 4x4 microkernel and the fringe path; preserve first-reduction-block zero initialization so every output is overwritten on each call.
